title: Signals
summary: Signals are generated, blocked, delivered and handled as POSIX specifies, including realtime signals, interval timers and job control.

cases.title: Signals whose default action is to terminate end the process with that signal in its wait status
Signals whose default action is to terminate with a core end the process with that signal in its wait status
SIGCHLD, SIGURG and SIGWINCH are ignored by default
SIGSTOP, SIGTSTP, SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU stop the process by default, reported by WUNTRACED with the signal
SIGCONT sent to a running process with the default action leaves it running
Signals set to SIG_IGN, including terminal stop and realtime signals, have no effect
Setting SIG_IGN discards a pending signal, even a blocked one
Setting SIG_DFL after a handler restores the default action
sigaction returns the previous handler, mask and flags, and a null action only queries
sigaction of signal 0, a negative signal or one above 64 fails with EINVAL
SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be caught or ignored (EINVAL) and report SIG_DFL
Linux ABI: rt_sigaction takes struct sigaction as handler, flags, restorer, mask
kill with signal 0 succeeds for a live process and a zombie, and fails with ESRCH once it is reaped
kill with an invalid signal number fails with EINVAL
kill of a missing process or process group fails with ESRCH
kill(-pgid) signals every member of that process group and no other process
kill(0) signals every member of the caller's process group, the caller included
kill(-1) as non-root signals every process of the caller's user and none of another user
kill as non-root fails with EPERM for another user's process and works for its own
SIGCONT may be sent to another user's process in the caller's session
A child inherits handlers and ignored signals, and handles a signal on a CoW stack with an unpopulated frame page
exec resets caught signals to SIG_DFL and keeps ignored ones ignored
A blocked signal stays pending and is delivered before sigprocmask returns once unblocked
A blocked signal stays pending across system calls, sleeps and yields
Linux policy: a standard signal sent by kill five times while blocked is delivered once
SIG_BLOCK adds to the mask, SIG_UNBLOCK removes from it, SIG_SETMASK replaces it, and each returns the old mask
sigprocmask with an invalid how fails with EINVAL and leaves the mask unchanged
sigprocmask with a null set ignores how and reports the mask
SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be blocked and still kill and stop
sigpending reports exactly the blocked signals that are pending
Unblocking two pending signals delivers both
pthread_sigmask in one thread leaves another thread's mask alone
A new thread starts with its creator's signal mask
A signal sent to the process is delivered to a thread that does not block it
pthread_kill delivers a signal to the thread it names
A child inherits its parent's signal mask
A child starts with no pending signals and the parent's stay pending
exec keeps the signal mask and the pending signals
A signal pending across exec is delivered with its default action once the new program unblocks it
A handler runs with the signal number before kill to the caller returns
An SA_SIGINFO handler gets si_signo, si_code SI_USER, si_pid, si_uid and a context
SA_SIGINFO reports the sending process's PID and real user ID
A fault on an unmapped address gives SIGSEGV with SEGV_MAPERR and the address in si_addr
SA_RESETHAND resets the action to SIG_DFL on entry to the handler, so the handler runs once
A signal is blocked while its own handler runs and unblocked when it returns
sa_mask is blocked while the handler runs and unblocked when it returns
With SA_NODEFER the signal raised in its own handler interrupts it
Without SA_NODEFER the signal raised in its own handler runs after it returns
A different signal raised in a handler runs its own handler inside it
Returning from a handler restores the mask it interrupted, undoing the handler's sigprocmask
A blocking read interrupted by an SA_RESTART handler is restarted
A blocking read interrupted by a handler without SA_RESTART fails with EINTR
A caught signal interrupts nanosleep with EINTR and the time left, even with SA_RESTART
waitpid interrupted by an SA_RESTART handler is restarted
waitpid interrupted by a handler without SA_RESTART fails with EINTR
General registers survive handlers that interrupt code holding them
Every floating-point and SIMD register, and the FP control and status state, survive handlers that overwrite them, nested or not; a handler's edit to the saved FP image takes effect
A process spinning in user mode, with no system call, on another processor runs its handler
sigsuspend returns EINTR after the handler and restores the mask
A signal already pending when sigsuspend unblocks it ends the wait at once with its handler run
A signal blocked by sigsuspend's mask does not end the wait and is delivered after it
A default-action terminating signal ends a process in sigsuspend
An ignored signal does not end sigsuspend
pause returns EINTR after a handler runs
A child's signal sent before the parent waits is caught by mask-then-sigsuspend
100 rounds of a child signalling while the parent enters sigsuspend lose no signal
sigtimedwait accepts a pending signal with its siginfo, without running the handler
sigtimedwait with nothing pending fails with EAGAIN after its timeout
sigtimedwait with a zero timeout and nothing pending fails with EAGAIN at once
sigtimedwait with an invalid timeout fails with EINVAL
sigwaitinfo waits for a signal sent by another process and reports its sender
A caught signal outside the set interrupts sigtimedwait with EINTR
alarm(1) delivers SIGALRM about a second later
SIGALRM from alarm with the default action terminates the process
alarm(0) returns the seconds left and cancels the alarm
A one-shot ITIMER_REAL delivers SIGALRM on time and getitimer reports the time left
A periodic ITIMER_REAL keeps delivering SIGALRM, no more often than its interval
setitimer returns the previous value and disarming leaves getitimer at zero
getitimer and setitimer fail with EINVAL for an unknown timer or an invalid time
ITIMER_VIRTUAL counts CPU time, not sleep, and delivers SIGVTALRM after the process computes for its interval
ITIMER_PROF counts CPU time, not sleep, and delivers SIGPROF after the process computes for its interval
A process starts with its alternate stack disabled
sigaltstack installs a stack and reads it back
A stack smaller than MINSIGSTKSZ fails with ENOMEM
An undefined ss_flags value fails with EINVAL
An SA_ONSTACK handler runs on untouched anonymous and private file stacks, which report SS_ONSTACK only while active
A handler without SA_ONSTACK runs on the normal stack
Changing or disabling the alternate stack while running on it fails with EPERM
SS_DISABLE disables the stack and SA_ONSTACK handlers run on the normal stack
After a stack overflow, the SIGSEGV handler runs on the alternate stack
A signal nested in an alternate-stack handler runs further down the same alternate stack
A new thread does not inherit its creator's alternate stack
exec leaves the new program with no alternate stack
Every realtime signal from 32 to 64 can be caught, blocked, held pending and delivered
A realtime signal sent by sigqueue five times while blocked, to an SA_SIGINFO handler, is delivered five times
Linux policy: a realtime signal sent by kill five times while blocked is delivered five times
Pending realtime signals are delivered lowest-numbered first
A realtime signal with the default action terminates the process
A realtime signal sent by kill reports SI_USER and the sender
sigqueue delivers its value with SI_QUEUE and the sender
Queued instances of one realtime signal arrive in the order sent, each with its value
sigqueue of a standard signal delivers its value with SI_QUEUE
sigqueue fails with ESRCH and EINVAL, and signal 0 checks the target
Linux ABI: with RLIMIT_SIGPENDING lowered to 64, sigqueue fails with EAGAIN at that limit, after at least 32, and every queued signal is delivered
sigtimedwait takes realtime signals queued by sigqueue one at a time, in order, with their values
A stopped process does not run until SIGCONT, and waitpid reports the stop and the continue
A signal sent to a stopped process is delivered after SIGCONT, not before
SIGKILL ends a stopped process
A caught SIGTSTP runs its handler and does not stop the process
SIGTSTP, SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU do not stop a process in an orphaned process group
SIGCONT continues a stopped process even when blocked or ignored
SIGCONT discards a pending stop signal
A child's exit raises SIGCHLD with CLD_EXITED, its PID and exit status
A child killed by a signal raises SIGCHLD with CLD_KILLED and the signal
A child's stop and continue raise SIGCHLD with CLD_STOPPED and CLD_CONTINUED
With SA_NOCLDSTOP a child's stop and continue raise no SIGCHLD, but its exit does
With SA_NOCLDWAIT an exited child leaves no zombie and waitpid fails with ECHILD
waitid reports CLD_STOPPED, CLD_CONTINUED and CLD_EXITED with their signals and status
kill(-pgid) with SIGSTOP and SIGCONT stops and continues every member
SIGSTOP stops every thread of a process computing on two processors, and SIGCONT resumes them
